problem: Valorant black screen / stuck loading bar on launch caused by Nahimic (A-Volute) audio service hooking (ProductInfo.dll)
symptoms: Valorant opens to black window with loading cursor, no audio, never reaches loading screen
Stuck at 10% red progress bar or infinite loading bar
VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe not responding; Alt+Enter does nothing
Sudden onset after a Valorant/Vanguard/Windows update on laptops (Lenovo LOQ/Legion, MSI, ASUS, Alienware)
Stutter + loading cursor + FPS halving in matches (one case)
Event Viewer: Faulting module ProductInfo.dll_unloaded, exception 0xc0000005 (one case 'incompatible software' popup)
root_causes: Nahimic/A-Volute audio-enhancement service (ProductInfo.dll) injects into the game and conflicts with Vanguard after a recent update
Nahimic gets reinstalled by Windows Update/OEM utilities after uninstall

fixes.fix: Stop and disable the 'Nahimic service' (services.msc -> Nahimic Service -> Startup type Disabled -> Stop; or Task Manager Services tab -> stop; or msconfig Services tab untick) then relaunch/restart PC
Fully uninstall Nahimic and restart (needed in some cases where only stopping did not clear the 10% hang); Windows Update may reinstall it
After disabling Nahimic install FXSound as an audio-enhancer replacement; commenters advise against uninstalling because it causes issues
Set vgc service Startup type to Automatic, restart PC, launch Riot Client as Administrator (OP of 1wcto1j confirmed; others said it did not help)
Run VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe and shortcut as administrator + disable fullscreen optimizations (one commenter said it worked)
Turn on Core Isolation (Memory integrity), reboot, launch Valorant, then turn it off again and reboot
Remove Lenovo Vantage together with Nahimic (not confirmed; one OP said it did not work)

diagnostic_signals: Event log Application: VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe faulting module ProductInfo.dll_unloaded, 0xc0000005
vgc service startup type (should be Automatic)

problem: Valorant micro-stutters/freezes caused by Realtek 2.5GbE (RTL8125/Gaming 2.5GbE) LAN controller driver
symptoms: Frame spike / freeze every 2-7 seconds only in Valorant, FPS counter drops, sometimes a 'bzz' sound or Windows beep
Ping/RTT jitter spikes about every 3-7 seconds, whole-system stutter even in Windows
Freezes/PC hangs on AMD builds (9070, 7800X3D, RX 9060XT); FPS falls from 1000 to 300-600
Occurs on both Ethernet and Wi-Fi in some reports
root_causes: Buggy Realtek Gaming 2.5GbE Family Controller / RTL8111H driver (Hardware IO error in System event log) triggered when Valorant/Vanguard runs, often on Windows 11 and AMD boards

fixes.fix: Device Manager -> Network adapters -> disable 'Realtek Gaming 2.5GbE / PCIe GbE Family Controller' (works when playing over Wi-Fi; on boards with two ports disable the second 2.5GbE one)
If on Ethernet: use a USB-to-Ethernet adapter with its own driver and disable the onboard Realtek controller
Update BIOS and the LAN driver from the motherboard vendor (Realtek Win10/Win11 Auto Installation Program NDIS); check Event Viewer System log for 'Realtek ... Hardware IO error'
Disable MPO (multiplane overlay) in NVIDIA and remove CPU 0 affinity for VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe (OP of 1vjv7ct confirmed this fixed it)
Full network reset in Windows settings

diagnostic_signals: Network adapter list contains Realtek 2.5GbE / RTL8125 / RTL8111H
Event log System: Realtek ... Hardware IO error / adapter reset when Valorant is open
Valorant frame-time spikes at regular interval; ping jitter graph periodic

problem: Valorant stutter linked to TPM events 14/17 (fTPM) in Event Viewer
symptoms: Constant stuttering in Valorant on Windows 11
System log shows TPM event 14 or 17 while playing
root_causes: fTPM firmware attestation issues (Vanguard TPM handshake); AMD fTPM firmware bug

fixes.fix: Disable TPM 2.0 in BIOS on Windows 10 (Win10 does not require TPM unless account is flagged) - guide author reports stutter gone; many commenters warn Win10 is unsupported and other users still had stutter
Update BIOS/AGESA containing TPM firmware update (B550 + 5800X reported fixed); set BIOS TPM to Auto instead of fTPM; or install a discrete TPM module
Disable MPO (suggested by commenter)

diagnostic_signals: Event log System TPM event IDs 14/17 during Valorant

problem: PC freezes/reboots or GPU driver crash/black screen only in Valorant (AMD Radeon driver regression, MPO, display config)
symptoms: PC freezes 1-2 minutes after entering the game/menu, then hard power-off or VGA debug LED
Screens go black, PC restarts, GPU shows disabled in Device Manager
Graphics driver timeout / 'Graphics driver crashed' after about a minute (RX 560, RX 7800 XT, 9060XT)
Black screen then forced restart (240Hz monitor with secondary monitor)
Display flicker and fallback to Microsoft Basic Display Adapter (MPO registry values clashing)
root_causes: Recent AMD Adrenalin drivers (26.5.2+/26.7.1/26.8.1) unstable with Valorant; downgrade to 26.1.1/26.3.1/26.6.1 helped some
Conflicting duplicate MPO-disable registry DWORD values after following two tutorials
Dual monitor + AMD scaling mode (GPU scaling off) causing crash
USB selective suspend causing hard lock on new PCs (Ryzen 9800X3D + RTX 5070 Ti)
Possibly failing GPU/VRAM (one 3080 with damaged VRAM)

fixes.fix: Disable USB selective suspend: Control Panel -> Power Options -> Change plan settings -> Advanced -> USB settings -> USB selective suspend -> Disabled, restart
Roll back/DDU-clean-install an older AMD driver (26.1.1, 26.3.1 or 26.6.1 reported); one user confirmed fix for a freeze, another saw it still crash after downgrade
In Adrenalin Settings -> Display enable GPU Scaling and set Scaling Mode to Full panel on both monitors (fixes crash with second monitor plugged)
Unplug secondary monitor and run main monitor at 120Hz instead of 240Hz (Riot games only)
Remove one of two conflicting MPO DWORD registry edits so the driver does not crash
Upgrade Windows 10 to Windows 11 (one commenter said it fixed the AMD driver crash)
Force iGPU in BIOS / Vanguard TPM attestation theory (OP's board had no option and root cause was MPO registry)
Valorant update itself fixed the 1-minute freeze on RX 9060 XT
Stress test GPU (FurMark), run VRAM test, check Event Viewer, DDU clean install

diagnostic_signals: Event log: display driver stopped responding (4101), Kernel-Power 41, LiveKernelEvent
Number of monitors and refresh rate

problem: VAN 185 - Vanguard disconnects / kicks player mid-match (network, adapter or antivirus conflict)
symptoms: Kicked from matches repeatedly with VAN 185 (4-5 times per match)
Game closes mid-match; Event Viewer shows vgc terminated unexpectedly
Random disconnect with VAN 185
root_causes: Wi-Fi connectivity/driver instability being flagged by Vanguard
Third-party antivirus (Quick Heal) killing Vanguard
Teredo tunneling adapter interfering (suggested)
Old low-end hardware overheating (suggested)

fixes.fix: Switch from Wi-Fi to wired Ethernet
Uninstall/disable Quick Heal antivirus (conflicts with Vanguard)
Wi-Fi adapter Advanced properties: 2.4G mode 802.11b/g/n/ax, 5G mode 802.11a/n/ac/ax, Preferred Band = Prefer 5G, Roaming Aggressiveness = Medium-Low, then restart
netsh interface teredo set state disabled (PowerShell)
Use Cloudflare WARP VPN (Riot reportedly told one commenter this works)
Set vgc service to Automatic, disable fullscreen optimizations, allow Vanguard through antivirus (earlier fix used by OP of 1vuavg9)

diagnostic_signals: vgc service status and startup type
Event log: vgc terminated unexpectedly / Service Control Manager 7023 Incorrect function
Connection type Wi-Fi and adapter model
Teredo state (netsh interface teredo show state)

problem: VAN 289 - Vanguard disconnect caused by conflicting VPN/anti-cheat software
symptoms: Game closes suddenly mid-game with VAN 289
Event Viewer vgc Event ID 7023 Incorrect function
root_causes: Internet-related apps (GlobalProtect VPN) or other anti-cheats (FACEIT) interfering with Vanguard

fixes.fix: Uninstall GlobalProtect and FACEIT anti-cheat (and other VPN/anticheat apps that can block Vanguard); OP reported solved after 2-3 games, durability unconfirmed
Try Cloudflare WARP or a different network (OP said no change)

problem: Vanguard error 136 / Discord freezing while playing Valorant (process priority)
symptoms: Valorant closes with error 136; Discord stuck loading or voice cuts out only while Valorant runs
root_causes: Setting Valorant to High priority lowers priority of important services, conflicting with Vanguard/Discord

fixes.fix: Set VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe (and Discord) priority to Normal/Above normal instead of High (Task Manager -> Details -> Set priority); OP confirmed Normal fixed everything
On low-end PCs if keyboard lag appears, uncheck CPU 0 and CPU 1 in Set affinity

diagnostic_signals: Process Lasso or startup scripts that raise priority

problem: Secure Boot cannot be enabled / boot loop back to BIOS (Vanguard requires Secure Boot)
symptoms: Enabling Secure Boot returns to BIOS repeatedly or shows 'invalid signature detected, check secure boot policy'
Vanguard says Secure Boot must be on after Windows update or CPU/motherboard swap
Boot menu loops
root_causes: Outdated BIOS (Gigabyte B450M DS3H F63 after Ryzen 5000 upgrade)
Corrupted Windows boot files / boot policy
Boot disk firmware or UEFI/GPT issues after motherboard swap

fixes.fix: Update motherboard BIOS (F67 stable, not beta F68a) then enable Secure Boot
Rebuild/install new Windows boot files (EFI partition) - OP fixed with AI guidance
Select Windows manually from boot menu, update SSD firmware, verify UEFI/GPT with diskpart and recreate UEFI boot via install media, mbr2gpt (none worked for the OP)

diagnostic_signals: BIOS mode UEFI vs Legacy, disk GPT vs MBR (diskpart / Get-Disk)

problem: VAN 9005 TPM 2.0 / VBS-HVCI loop on Windows 10 and Memory Integrity turning itself off
symptoms: Game still demands TPM 2.0 on Windows 10 after a patch asked to enable HVCI/VBS, never-ending loop
Memory Integrity (HVCI) disables itself after restart when VT-d enabled (ASUS Z490-E)
VAN9002 CFG requirement message
root_causes: Vanguard requires Secure Boot + current Windows + HVCI/VBS state coherent
Newer ASUS Z490-E BIOS versions break HVCI persistence with VT-d

fixes.fix: Enable Secure Boot (UEFI), update Windows 10 fully, then turn Memory Integrity off in Core isolation and restart
Roll back ASUS ROG STRIX Z490-E BIOS to version 3201 so Memory Integrity stays enabled

problem: Vanguard 'system restart required' loop each boot
symptoms: Riot Client shows 'Your game requires a system restart to play' every boot, restart does not fix it
root_causes: Unknown; vgk driver not loading cleanly (antivirus suspected)

fixes.fix: Uninstall and reinstall Vanguard; check for antivirus

problem: Regional ping spike / routing problems (Frankfurt, Sydney-Singapore, Germany-Turkey, Middle East)
symptoms: Sudden +15 to +40 ms ping or packet loss to a specific Riot server only
Ping jumped from 100 to 180 ms Sydney to Singapore
200ms to Riyadh from Kuwait with 400-1000ms spikes
root_causes: ISP routing change or damaged submarine cable (AUS-SEA cable), not a local fault
Wi-Fi jitter (rubber-banding)

fixes.fix: Wait: issue self-resolved after hours/days (Frankfurt, German ISP routing 18 Sept, reported to Riot support)
Switch to a nearby server (Tokyo instead of Singapore) as workaround
Rubber-banding fixed by switching Wi-Fi to 4G/mobile connection; ExitLag route (paid) suggested for routing

diagnostic_signals: Ping/traceroute/packet loss to Riot servers (Frankfurt, Singapore, etc.)
Compare ping of other games and mobile hotspot

problem: Packet loss/bufferbloat - switch TCP congestion provider to BBR2
symptoms: Packet loss/bufferbloat, slow downloads
root_causes: Default CUBIC congestion provider causing bufferbloat (author's belief; commenters doubt Valorant gameplay uses TCP)

fixes.fix: netsh int tcp set supplemental Template=Internet|Datacenter|Compat|DatacenterCustom|InternetCustom CongestionProvider=bbr2; netsh int ipv4/ipv6 set gl loopbacklargemtu=disable; revert by setting CUBIC

problem: Valorant voice chat not working / robotic after update
symptoms: Voice comms stopped after update, teammates appear muted
Voice robotic/choppy, party or team chat intermittently broken while Discord is fine
root_causes: IPv6 handling in Vivox voice connection
Vivox routing/provider issues; overlays and hardware-accelerated apps (Spotify/Discord/Opera) interfering

fixes.fix: Disable IPv6 on the network adapter
Turn off all overlays (Discord, NVIDIA) and hardware acceleration in Spotify/Discord/Opera
Riot support list: wired Ethernet, IPv4 only, Google/Cloudflare DNS, ipconfig /release /renew, flushdns, update NIC driver, power cycle modem, disable KillerNetworkService

problem: Mouse sensitivity feels floaty/faster in Valorant
symptoms: Sens suddenly feels fast after resetting monitor
Crosshair floaty after update, even with new mouse/laptop
Mouse lag when moving
root_causes: Enhanced pointer precision turned on
Possible post-update FPS/CPU-limited input latency (unconfirmed)

fixes.fix: Turn off Enhance pointer precision in Windows mouse settings (OP found it was on)
Check mouse polling rate 500/1000Hz, lower graphics settings

diagnostic_signals: Windows MouseAcceleration / Enhance pointer precision registry (HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse MouseSpeed)

problem: Mouse clicks stop working after Alt-Tab and random Valorant crashes
symptoms: Left/right click not registering after tabbing out until Task Manager is opened
Random game crashes on fresh Windows install with 3600MHz RAM on Ryzen 7 3700X
root_causes: Mouse button 4 (Browser Back) causing Windows focus bug
RAM at 3600MHz beyond memory controller stability

fixes.fix: Rebind MB4 in iCUE so it does not send Browser Back
Keep DOCP enabled but manually adjust memory settings for stability (OP post truncated)

diagnostic_signals: RAM speed vs CPU official spec

problem: FPS drop/decay over time or FPS counter at half of cap
symptoms: FPS slowly falls during the session on AMD 9070XT/9800X3D
FPS counter shows half of the set limit (120 for 240)
FPS drops/crashes after new Act update on weak laptop
root_causes: Windowed fullscreen mode behavior
New NVIDIA driver
Valorant patch regression

fixes.fix: Switch from Windowed Fullscreen to Fullscreen in video settings
Roll back to previous NVIDIA Game Ready driver
Riot patch fixed FPS drops after update
Lower resolution then raise fps cap gradually (60->80->100) fixed crash on i5-4460/RX 560
Close overlays like Overwolf; check temps; Process Lasso high priority

problem: Stutter due to RTSS (RivaTuner) overlay or AMD shader cache / Adrenalin cap settings
symptoms: Stuttering and unable to cap FPS on RX 9060XT/Ryzen 5 7600
Stutter every few seconds on RX 6800 / DX11 AMD
root_causes: RTSS injection even on low detection
AMD shader cache not built (Valorant DX11)
Adrenalin setting ignoring fps cap

fixes.fix: Turn off RTSS entirely (stutter gone)
Reset AMD Adrenalin settings to default fixes FPS cap not working
Play several matches/Swiftplay to rebuild shader cache, stay on one driver, reset shader cache; disable Anti-Lag

problem: Valorant freezes while in lobby / on MSI X3D Game Mode
symptoms: Game freezes for a couple of seconds in lobby every few minutes (7800X3D, 4070)
root_causes: MSI BIOS X3D Gaming Mode restricts logical processors (disputed - happens on non-X3D too)

fixes.fix: Disable X3D gaming mode in MSI BIOS

diagnostic_signals: BIOS vendor MSI and X3D mode

problem: Valorant fails to launch / stuck at loading due to conflicting software (National Instruments)
symptoms: Stuck on loading screen for months on ThinkPad, secure boot fine
root_causes: National Instruments software conflicts with Vanguard

fixes.fix: Uninstall National Instruments software

problem: Game crashes on settings/queue - outdated Intel iGPU/chipset driver
symptoms: Crash when opening settings or queueing after character select
root_causes: Outdated driver not installed by NVIDIA update on Intel laptop

fixes.fix: Download Intel Driver & Support Assistant and clean install all drivers

problem: Display issues: monitor not shown, resolution locked, stretched res, UI pixelation, tearing, blurry HUD
symptoms: Valorant not showing main monitor
Resolution stuck on native after Valorant opens
True stretched shows black bars
UI icons pixelate
Screen tearing on Lenovo LOQ unless VSync on
Blurry HUD on mouse movement (RX 7600)
root_causes: Monitor disabled in Device Manager
Wrong resolution chosen
Corrupt install

fixes.fix: Re-enable the monitor in Device Manager
Fixed by selecting the correct resolution (user had wrong res)
Reinstall Valorant for pixelated UI
Windowed fullscreen / check NVIDIA settings for tearing (not confirmed)

diagnostic_signals: Current display mode and refresh rate

problem: Slow Valorant download (1.1MB/s)
symptoms: Download stuck at 1.1MB/s despite fast connection
root_causes: Riot CDN issue

fixes.fix: Wait, resolved by itself next morning (Riot-side); pause/resume and VPN suggested

diagnostic_signals: Download speed to Riot CDN vs other services

problem: Valorant version mismatch / unable to install
symptoms: VALORANT VERSION MISMATCH after reinstalling Riot Client, Vanguard, repair
diagnostic_signals: Riot Client/Vanguard version and patch state
